content:
Gabe: Quick recap for folks who asked for dates during today's all-hands. Putting the short answers here and who owns each item.

Leah: API gen2 runtime: internal canary this week, partner canary ~3w after, GA about 6w after partner canary. It'll be opt-in via `api_version=gen2` for pinned models. No forced cutover.

Isha: Will streaming payloads change? Any webhook consumers affected?

Leah: Streaming framing improved (more incremental function-arg chunks). Backwards compatibility for 90 days after GA; we'll publish migration snippets for webhook consumers.

Tom: Dedicated/Private ops impact? Customers want maintenance windows spelled out.

Leah: Dedicated: control-plane first, then rolling node updates with live migration where possible. Private customers get an upgrade package and checklist to run on their schedule. We'll provide per-customer windows and notices.

Rhea: Console features timeline? Folks expect per-route cost and rollout controls.

Leah: Console beta (internal + pilot partners) mid-April, public opt-in beta mid-May, GA end of Q2. Beta includes per-route token cost, latency percentiles, and basic canary UI with quick rollback.

Gabe: Optimize specifics: batching suggestions vs quantization timing?

Leah: Batching/caching advisor: internal alpha in ~2 sprints, public alpha by month-end. Quantization recommender (with quality estimates) targeted for Q3. We'll release an RFC and sample evals ahead of public launches.

DeployBot: "canary-start: api/gen2-runtime -> alpha at 1998765475"

Gabe: Action items: 1) @Leah publish timeline + migration checklist tomorrow AM. 2) @Isha to coordinate SDK patches and examples. 3) @Tom to prepare Dedicated maintenance notice templates. 4) Product to publish beta invite process.

Leah: I'll post the doc in #eng and update public roadmap.

Isha: I'll open Python/JS PRs right after the internal canary and add sample webhook code.

Tom: I'll sync with CS and send template language by EOD.

Gabe: If anyone had a question during the panel that's not captured, paste it here and we'll route it. Thanks :rocket:
